Surah Ta-Ha [Meccan, except verses 120 and 121, which are Medinan. Its verses number 135, or 40, or 2. It was revealed after Maryam.]

﴿Ta-Ha﴾ God knows best what He means by this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 2:

﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you﴾ O Muhammad (ﷺ) ﴿to make you suffer﴾ to make you exert yourself because of what you did after its revelation, through your prolonged standing in the night prayer; i.e., lighten it upon yourself.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 20, verse 3:

﴿Illā﴾ [meaning] but ﴿We sent it down as a reminder﴾ with it, ﴿for those who fear﴾ Allah.

﴿A revelation﴾ is a substitute (*badal*) for the word, with its governing verb (*nāṣib*) understood: ﴿from He who created the earth and the high heavens﴾. ﴿Al-ʿulā﴾ is the plural of ﴿ʿulyā﴾, like ﴿kubar﴾ is the plural of ﴿kubrā﴾.

He is "the Most Merciful, above the Throne" ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ ... "the Throne" (ʿarsh) in the language means the royal seat (sarīr al-mulk). ﴿istawā﴾: He rose over it in a manner befitting Him (istiwāʾ yalīq bihi).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 6:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them﴾ of the created things, ﴿and whatever is beneath the soil﴾ it is the moist earth, and what is meant is the seven earths, because they are beneath it.

﴿And if you speak aloud﴾ in remembrance or supplication, then Allah is free of any need for the loudness of it, ﴿for He knows the secret and what is yet more hidden﴾ than it, i.e., what the self speaks to itself and what occurs to it without being voiced. So do not strain yourself with loudness.

﴿Allah, there is no god except Him. To Him belong the most beautiful names.﴾ They are the ninety-nine (names) mentioned in the hadith (prophetic tradition). Al-husna is the feminine form of al-ahsan (the most beautiful).
﴿وهَلْ﴾ (here meaning) qad

When Moses saw a fire and said to his family, ﴿Stay here; I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you a burning brand from it, or find at the fire guidance.﴾ [The family, i.e.] to his wife, "Stay here," that is, here. This was during his journey from Madyan, heading for Egypt. "I have perceived," i.e., I have seen, "a fire." "Perhaps I will bring you from it a brand," i.e., a firebrand on the end of a wick or a stick. He said "perhaps" (la'alla) because of the lack of certainty in fulfilling the promise. "Or find at the fire guidance," i.e., a guide who would show me the way; he had missed the fire because of the darkness of the night.
﴿When he came to it﴾, and it was an 'awsaj tree.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 12:

﴿Indeed, I﴾ — with the hamza of "innī" pronounced with a kasra, on the interpretation that it is the verb "nūdiya" (it was called out) in the sense of "qīla" (it was said); and with a fatha, on the assumption of a preposition "bi-" before it (i.e., "bi-annī," "that I"). ﴿am your Lord﴾ — "anā" is an emphatic restatement of the pronoun of the speaker (the "yā'" of "innī" and "rabbuka"). ﴿So take off your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley﴾ — the purified or the blessed one. ﴿Tuwā﴾ — it is either a substitute (badal) or an explanatory appositive (ʿaṭf bayān). With tanwīn it is diptote-free (munṣarif), considering it as the name of a place; and without tanwīn it is non-declinable (ghayr munṣarif), due to its feminine sense considering it as a locality, together with its being a proper name.
"And I have chosen you" from among your people, "so listen to what is revealed" to you from Me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 14:

﴿Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.﴾ For My remembrance in it (i.e., in the prayer).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 15:

﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it﴾ from the people, and its nearness appears to them through its signs. ﴿So that every soul may be recompensed﴾ therein ﴿for what it strives﴾ toward, of good or of evil.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 16:

﴿So let not one who does not believe in it and follows his desire turn you away from it, lest you perish﴾ — yaṣrifannaka (turn you away) ﴿from it﴾, i.e., from belief in it ﴿—one who does not believe in it and follows his desire﴾ in denying it ﴿—lest you perish﴾, i.e., lest you be destroyed if you are turned away from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 17:

﴿And what is that﴾ — the interrogative is for confirmation (taqrir), so that the miracle in it may be built upon it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 18:

﴿He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it﴾ (a'tamid) ﴿on it﴾ when rising up and walking, ﴿and I beat down﴾ (akhbit) ﴿with it the leaves of the trees﴾ ﴿so that they fall﴾ ﴿upon my sheep﴾ so that they eat them, ﴿and I have in it other uses﴾" (maarib), the plural of ma'ruba (with the ra' vowelled in three ways), meaning needs ﴿other﴾, such as carrying provisions and water-skins and driving away pests. He added to the answer an explanation of his needs with it.

﴿So he threw it down, and behold, it was a serpent﴾ , a great snake, ﴿moving swiftly﴾, going along on its belly quickly, like the speed of the small serpent called the jann, which is referred to by this word in another verse.

Qur'an quotation: ﴿He said: "Take it and fear not; We shall restore it to its former state"﴾. Here "sīratahā" is accusative by removal of the preposition (naz' al-khāfid), meaning "to its state" (ilā ḥālatihā), "the first" (al-ūlā).

So he put his hand into its mouth, and it returned to being a staff. It became clear that the place of insertion was the place where he grasped it, between its two prongs (shu'batayhā). That was shown to the Master (al-sayyid), Mūsā, so that he would not be alarmed if it turned into a snake before Pharaoh.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 22:

﴿And draw your hand﴾ [the right one] (al-yumna), meaning the palm (al-kaff), ﴿to your side﴾, i.e., your left side, beneath the upper arm (al-'adud) down to the armpit (al-ibt), ﴿and it will come out﴾ [i.e., come forth] ﴿white, without blemish﴾, contrary to what it had been of its natural complexion (al-adama), ﴿[white] without harm﴾, i.e., leprosy (baras), shining like the rays of the sun that dazzle the sight, ﴿as another sign﴾, and it is ﴿white﴾, two circumstantial phrases (hal) referring to the pronoun in ﴿will come out﴾.

"So that We may show you of Our greater signs."

Explanation: (with it) when you do that, to display it. "Of Our signs" — the verse. "The greatest" — i.e., the greatest proof of your prophethood. And when he wanted it to return to its former state, he drew it to his side (jinah), as mentioned before, and it came out.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 24:

﴿Go﴾ as a messenger ﴿to Pharaoh﴾ and those with him, ﴿for he has transgressed﴾, going beyond the limit in his disbelief to the claim of divinity.
﴿He said, "My Lord, expand for me my breast"﴾ — widen it for bearing the message.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 20, verse 26:

﴿And ease for me﴾ make easy ﴿my affair﴾ so that I may convey it.
And loosen the knot from my tongue. (That knot) came about from its being burned by an ember which he placed in his mouth when he was a child.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 28:

﴿that they may understand﴾ yafhamu ﴿my speech﴾ at the time of conveying (tabligh) the message

"And appoint for me a minister" — helping me in it (ﷺ no; text) 

Translation:

﴿And appoint for me a minister﴾ — an assistant helping me with it.
Harun (هارُون) is the second object, and "my brother" (أخِي) is an explicative apposition (عطف بيان).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 31:

﴿Strengthen my back with him (ushdud bihi azri)﴾ And the two verbs are in the imperative form and the jussive present form, and the latter is the answer to the imperative (jawab al-talab).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 32:

﴿And make him a partner in my affair﴾, i.e., in the prophethood (al-risala). The two verbs are in the imperative form (amr) and the jussive present (mudari' majzum) form, and the latter is the answer (jawab) to the imperative (talab).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 33:

﴿So that we may glorify You﴾ with much glorification
﴿And [that] We may remember You﴾ abundantly
﴿Indeed You have always been, of us, Seeing﴾, knowing, so You favoured us with the message.
﴿He said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses."﴾ [This is a favour] from Us to you.

﴿Idh﴾ is for ta'lil (giving a reason), ﴿We inspired to your mother﴾ either in a dream or by inspiration (ilham) when she gave birth to you and feared that Pharaoh would kill you along with the other newborns, ﴿what is inspired﴾ concerning your matter, and ﴿what is inspired﴾ is a substitute (badal) for it.

﴿That cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river﴾: "cast him" means put him in the chest; "cast it" means the chest, into the river (yamm), the Nile.

﴿Then let the river throw him onto the bank﴾: its shore. The imperative here carries the sense of a report.

﴿An enemy to Me and an enemy to him will take him﴾: this is Pharaoh.

﴿And I cast upon you﴾, after He took you, ﴿love from Me﴾, so that you would be loved among people, and so Pharaoh loved you, as did everyone who saw you.

﴿And that you might be raised under My eye﴾: brought up under My care and protection for you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 40:

﴿Idh﴾ (is) for causation (ta'lil). ﴿Your sister walks﴾, Maryam, so that she may learn of your news, and they had brought wet-nurses while you would not accept the breast of any one of them. ﴿Then she said: "Shall I direct you to someone who will nurse him?"﴾ She was answered, so she came with his mother, and he accepted her breast. ﴿So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted﴾ by meeting you, ﴿and that she should not grieve﴾ at that time. ﴿And you killed a soul﴾, namely the Copt in Egypt, and you were distressed over killing him on account of Pharaoh. ﴿Then We delivered you from distress and tested you with a testing﴾, We tried you by being thrown into other than that, and We rescued you from it. ﴿Then you stayed for years﴾, ten, ﴿among the people of Madyan﴾ after your arrival there from Egypt, with Shu'ayb the Prophet, and your marriage to his daughter. ﴿Then you came, O Moses, at a predestined time﴾ in My knowledge for the message, and that was when you were forty years old.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 41:

﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾ (ightakhartuka) I selected you ﴿for Myself﴾ with the message (bi-l-risala).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 42:

﴿Go, you and your brother,﴾ to the people, ﴿with My signs﴾ the nine, ﴿and do not slacken﴾ do not become lax, ﴿in remembering Me﴾ by glorifying (tasbih) and other than it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 43:

﴿Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed﴾ by his claim to lordship (rububiyya)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 44:

﴿Then speak to him with gentle speech,﴾ (so that he might turn back from that) ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or fear (Allah),﴾ that is, he will take heed, and fear (Allah) and so turn back. The expression of hope (la'alla, "perhaps") is with reference to the two of them (Moses and Aaron), since He, exalted is He, knows that he will not turn back.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 45:

﴿They said: "Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us with punishment"﴾ — i.e., he will hasten to punish us — ﴿or that he will transgress against us﴾ — i.e., he will become arrogant toward us.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 46:

﴿He said: "Do not fear; indeed I am with you both"﴾ with My help, ﴿hearing﴾ what he says ﴿and seeing﴾ what he does.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 47:

﴿So go to him and say: "We are both messengers of your Lord, so send the Children of Israel with us [to al-Sham]. And do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace be upon whoever follows the guidance."﴾

[to al-Sham]: to the Levant (al-Sham).

﴿And do not torment them﴾: i.e., release them from your employing them in your arduous tasks, such as digging, building and carrying heavy loads.

﴿We have come to you with a sign﴾: with a proof ﴿from your Lord﴾ confirming the truth of our message.

﴿And peace be upon whoever follows the guidance﴾: i.e., safety from punishment for him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 48:

﴿Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon him who denies﴾ what we have brought, ﴿and turns away﴾ from it, [i.e., turns away from it]. ﴿So they both came to him and said﴾ all of what has been mentioned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 49:

﴿He said, "Then who is your Lord, O Moses?"﴾ He limited the question to this because it is the principal matter, and because of Pharaoh's presumption that he had a claim over him through upbringing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 50:

﴿He said: "Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation﴾ from among the creatures, ﴿the form﴾ that it has, by which it is distinguished from other than it, ﴿then guided﴾ the animals among them to their food, their drink, their mating, and other things."
Pharaoh said, ﴿What then is the case of the earlier generations?﴾ (i.e., the condition of the former peoples), ﴿such as the people of Noah, Hud, Lut and Salih in their worship of idols?﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 52:

﴿Mūsā said﴾ "Their knowledge" — i.e., the knowledge of their state — "is preserved with my Lord in a Book," which is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), "He will recompense them for it on the Day of Resurrection. My Lord does not err" — i.e., is not absent from — "anything, nor does He forget" anything.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 53:

﴿Who has made for you﴾ within the totality of creation, ﴿the earth a cradle﴾, a bed-spread, ﴿and has threaded﴾ made easy, ﴿for you therein roads﴾ paths, ﴿and sent down from the sky water﴾ rain. Exalted is He, said as a completion of what Moses described Him with, and as an address to the people of Makkah. ﴿Then We brought forth thereby pairs﴾ kinds, ﴿of plants diverse﴾ an adjective of "pairs," meaning differing in colours, tastes and other qualities. And "shattā" (diverse) is the plural of "shatīt," like "marīḍ" and "marḍā" (sick), from "shatta al-amr," meaning it scattered (dispersed).

Eat (﴿kulu﴾) from them, and graze your livestock (﴿wa-r'aw an'amakum﴾) among them. An-'Am (livestock) is the plural of na'am, which means camels, cattle and sheep; one says ra'at al-an'am and ra'aytuha (they grazed the livestock, and I grazed them). The imperative here is for permission, and it serves to remind of the blessing. The clause is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring back to the pronoun in akhrajna, meaning: permitting you to eat and to graze your livestock. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ mentioned here ﴿are signs﴾, that is, lessons ﴿for people of understanding﴾, that is, for those possessing intellects. Nuha is the plural of nuhya, like ghurfa and ghuraf. Reason (al-'aql) is so named because it restrains (yanha) its possessor from committing ugly deeds (al-qaba'ih).

From it We created you, and into it We return you, and from it We bring you forth once again.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on this verse:

﴿Minha﴾ (from it), i.e., from the earth: ﴿khalaqnakum﴾ (We created you) through the creation of your father Adam, who was made from it. ﴿Wa-fiha nu'idukum﴾ (and into it We return you), buried in graves after death. ﴿Wa-minha nukhrijukum﴾ (and from it We bring you forth) at the Resurrection ﴿taratan ukhra﴾ (once again), a second time, ﴿kama akhrajnakum﴾ (as We brought you forth) at the beginning of your creation.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 56:**

﴿And We had certainly shown him﴾, i.e., We made Pharaoh see ﴿Our signs, all of them﴾, the nine ones, ﴿but he denied them﴾ and claimed that they were sorcery, ﴿and refused﴾ to affirm the Oneness of God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 57:

﴿He said: "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land"﴾ Egypt, "and for you to have the kingship in it?"

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 20, verse 58:

﴿So we will surely bring you magic like it,⁠ (i.e., one that will counter it)﴾ ﴿so set between us and you an appointment⁠ (for that)﴾ ﴿that we will not fail, neither we nor you, at a place⁠ (makan, accusative by removal of the preposition, with "suwan" [a place equidistant]), ﴾ with the initial letter pronounced with kasra or damma, i.e., a middle place, to which the distance of the one coming from either side is equal.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 59:

﴿Said﴾ Musa, ﴿Your appointment is the Day of Adornment﴾, a day of festival for them, when they adorn themselves and gather, ﴿and that the people be assembled﴾, the people of Egypt be gathered, ﴿in the forenoon﴾; he set it as the time for looking into what would take place.
﴿Then Pharaoh turned away﴾ meaning he withdrew, ﴿and gathered his scheming﴾ meaning, those of his scheme, from the magicians, ﴿then came﴾ with them to the appointment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 61:

﴿Musa said to them﴾ — and they were seventy-two men, each with a rope and a staff — ﴿Woe to you!﴾ — i.e., Allah will impose destruction (al-wayl) upon you — ﴿Do not fabricate a lie against Allah,﴾ by associating anyone with Him, ﴿lest He destroy you﴾ — with a dammah on the yaʾ and a kasrah on the ḥaʾ, and also with a fatḥah on both — i.e., annihilate you ﴿with a punishment﴾ from Him, ﴿and surely he fails﴾ — loses — ﴿who fabricates﴾ — lies — ﴿against Allah.﴾
﴿So they disputed their affair among themselves﴾ concerning Moses and his brother, ﴿and they secretly conferred﴾, i.e., they spoke together in secret about the two of them.

**﴿They said﴾** to one another: **﴿"Indeed, these two﴾** — this is in accordance with the dialect of those who write the dual with an alif in all its cases (*hadhān*, not *hadhayn*). According to Abu 'Amr, it is *hadhayn* — **﴿"are surely two sorcerers who wish to drive you out of your land by their magic and to abolish your best way of life"﴾**. *Al-muthlā* is the feminine of *amthal*, meaning "more noble," i.e., "your nobles." They said this because the people were inclined toward the two of them due to their dominance.

﴿So gather your plot﴾ of magic. (It may be read with a hamzat wasl (connecting hamza) and a fatḥa on the mīm, from jama'a, meaning to collect, or with a hamzat qaṭ' (cutting hamza) and a kasra on the mīm, from aj'ama, meaning to make firm.) ﴿Then come forward in a row﴾: this is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative), meaning arranged in ranks. ﴿And indeed he has succeeded today who prevails﴾: meaning won (fāza), and overcame (ghalaba).
They said, "O Moses, [you choose:] either you throw [your staff] first, or we will be the first to throw."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 66:

﴿He said: "Nay, you throw first."﴾ So they threw, ﴿and behold, their cords and their staffs,﴾ its original form was ʿuṣūw (عُصُوو), the two waws were changed into two yāʾs, and the ʿayn and the ṣād were given a kasra. ﴿It was imagined to him, by their magic, that they were﴾ serpents ﴿moving swiftly﴾ upon their bellies.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Tafsir of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 20, verse 67:

﴿فَأَوْجَسَ﴾ (So he sensed) أحَسَّ (he perceived) ﴿فِي نَفْسه خِيفَة مُوسى﴾ (within himself a fear, Musa) أيْ (i.e.) خافَ (he feared) مِن جِهَة أنَّ سِحْرهمْ (from the standpoint that their magic) مِن جِنْس مُعْجِزَته (is of the same kind as his miracle) أنْ يَلْتَبِس أمْره عَلى النّاس (that his affair would become confused for the people) فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ (so they would not believe in him)
"We said" to him, "Do not fear. Indeed you are the superior one" over them by victory.

"And throw what is in your right hand" — which is his staff — "it will swallow up" what they have made. "What they have made is only a magician's deception," that is, its kind. "And the magician does not prosper, wherever he comes from," with his magic. So Musa threw his staff, and it swallowed up everything they had made.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 70:

﴿So the sorcerers were thrown down prostrate﴾ they fell down prostrating themselves to Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 71:

﴿He said﴾ Pharaoh, ﴿Have you believed in him before I give you permission?﴾ (The first two hamzas are pronounced as two hamzas, with the second changed into an alif.) ﴿Indeed, he is your chief﴾ (your teacher) ﴿who taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾ (a circumstantial clause meaning "differing," i.e., the right hands and the left feet) ﴿and I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ (i.e., upon them). ﴿And you will surely know whose punishment is more severe and more lasting﴾ (he means himself and the Lord of Moses), ﴿more severe and more lasting﴾ (more enduring in its continuation).

They said, "We will never prefer you ﴿over what has come to us of the clear proofs﴾ [i.e., we will choose you over]... " 

Let me be precise and follow the instructions: translate the passage faithfully.

They said, "We will never prefer you" (nakhtaruka) "over what has come to us of the clear proofs" (al-bayyinat), which indicate the truthfulness of Musa (Moses), "and over He who originated us" (fatarana, i.e., created us). It is an oath, or it is conjoined to "what" (ma) [in "over what has come to us"]. "So decree what you will decree" (i.e., do what you have said). "You can only decree concerning this worldly life" — the accusative here is by way of extension (al-ittisa'), meaning "in it." "And you will be recompensed for it in the Hereafter."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 73:

﴿Indeed, we have believed in our Lord, that He may forgive us our sins﴾ of polytheism and other than it, ﴿and [forgive us] the magic to which you compelled us﴾ in learning and practising it, to oppose Musa, ﴿And Allah is better﴾ than you in reward if obeyed, ﴿and more enduring﴾ than you in punishment if disobeyed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 74:

﴿Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal﴾ (i.e., an unbeliever, like Pharaoh), ﴿for him is Hell; he will neither die therein﴾ so as to find rest, ﴿nor live﴾ a life that benefits him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 75:

﴿And whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done righteous deeds﴾ — the obligatory and the voluntary acts of worship — ﴿for them are the high ranks﴾ — the plural of ʿulyā (feminine of aʿlā, "highest").

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 20, verse 76:

﴿Gardens of perpetual residence (ʿAdn)﴾ i.e., a dwelling place, ﴿beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the recompense of him who purifies himself (tazakkā)﴾ i.e., who purifies himself from sins.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 77:

﴿And We certainly revealed to Musa: "Travel by night with My servants."﴾ With a cutting hamzah (ʾAsri, from asrā) and with a connecting hamzah and a kasrah on the nun (Sari, from sarā), there are two dialects, meaning: travel with them by night from the land of Egypt. ﴿Then strike for them﴾ make for them, by striking with your staff, ﴿a dry path through the sea﴾ i.e., dry (yābisan). So he carried out what he was commanded, and Allah dried the land, and they passed through it. ﴿Do not fear being overtaken﴾ i.e., that Fir'awn will overtake you, ﴿and do not dread﴾ drowning.

Pharaoh followed them with his armies (﴿فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْن بِجُنُودِهِ﴾), and he was with them (وهُوَ مَعَهُمْ). ﴿So the sea covered them, that which covered them﴾ (﴿فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِن اليَمّ﴾), i.e., the sea (أيْ البَحْر) ﴿that which covered them﴾ (﴿ما غَشِيَهُمْ﴾), so it drowned them (فَأَغْرَقَهُمْ).

﴿And Pharaoh led his people astray﴾ by calling them to worship him, ﴿and he did not guide them﴾ but rather brought them to destruction, contrary to his saying ﴿"I show you nothing but the way of right judgment"﴾.

O Children of Israel, We had certainly delivered you from your enemy (Pharaoh) by drowning him, and We made an appointment with you on the right side of the Mount (al-Tur), so that We would give Moses the Torah to act upon, and We sent down to you the manna and the quail (al-salwa). These are the terangbin (a sweet exudation, manna) and the migratory bird (al-tayr al-sumani, quail), with the mim lightened and the ending short (qasr). The one addressed is whoever of the Jews was present at the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they were addressed with what Allah bestowed upon their forefathers at the time of the Prophet Moses, as a preface to His saying, exalted is He, to them:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 81:

﴿Eat of the good things that We have provided you with﴾, i.e., the bounty bestowed upon you, ﴿but do not transgress therein﴾ by being ungrateful for the blessing through it, ﴿lest My wrath (ghadabi) descend upon you﴾. With the vowel of the ḥāʾ (ḥāʾ) kasra (yaḥilla, "is due"), i.e., it becomes incumbent; and with ḍamma (yaḥulla), i.e., it descends. ﴿And whoever has My wrath descend upon him﴾, with kasra and ḍamma on the lām (yaḥlil / yaḥull), ﴿has indeed fallen (hawā)﴾, i.e., has plunged into the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 82:

﴿And indeed, I am Forgiving toward those who repent﴾ from polytheism, ﴿and believe﴾ (i.e., affirm the oneness of God), ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ (this includes both obligatory and voluntary acts), ﴿then remain guided﴾ by persisting in what has been mentioned until his death.
﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ For the coming of the appointed time to receive the Tawrah (the Torah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 20, verse 84:

﴿He said, "They are right behind me"﴾, that is, close to me, coming ﴿in my footsteps﴾. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased﴾ with me, that is, an increase in Your pleasure. Before the answer came, he offered the excuse according to his assumption, and the non-fulfillment of what he had presumed when

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 85:

﴿He said﴾ [Allah, Exalted is He]: ﴿Indeed, We have tried your people after you﴾, i.e., after your departure from them, ﴿and the Samiri has led them astray﴾, so they worshipped the calf.

﴿So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾ over their conduct, ﴿deeply sorrowful﴾ (asafan), ﴿and said: "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise?"﴾ meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿"Did the time seem long to you?"﴾ referring to the period of my absence from you. ﴿"Or did you wish that wrath should descend"﴾ upon you through your worship of the calf ﴿"so that you broke your appointment with me?"﴾ and abandoned coming after me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 87:

﴿They said: "We did not break our promise to you of our own will"﴾ (the word "bi-mulkinā" may be read with three vowel patterns on the mīm), i.e., by our power or by our decision. ﴿"But we were made to carry loads"﴾ (the verb may be read with a light ḥāʾ and a fatḥah, or with a ḍammah, and with a shaddah on the mīm), i.e., burdens ﴿"of the ornaments of the people"﴾, i.e., the jewelry of the people of Pharaoh, which the Children of Israel had borrowed from them on the pretext of a wedding, and which then remained in their possession. ﴿"So we threw them"﴾, i.e., we cast them into the fire, at the command of al-Sāmirī. ﴿"Thus"﴾, as We cast them, ﴿"did al-Sāmirī cast"﴾ what he had with him of their jewelry, and of the dust that he had taken from the trace of the hoof of Gabriel's horse, in the manner that follows.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 88:

﴿So he brought forth for them a calf﴾ that he had fashioned from the ornaments, ﴿a body﴾ of flesh and blood, ﴿that lowed﴾, i.e., it made a sound that could be heard. That is, it was transformed in this way because of the dust (turab) whose trace is life in whatever it is placed in, and he placed it in its mouth after he had fashioned it. ﴿Then they said﴾, i.e., al-Samiri and his followers: ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he has forgotten﴾, meaning Musa has forgotten his Lord here and has gone off to seek Him.

﴿Will they not see﴾ that (أنْ) is the light form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy (thaqilah) one, and its subject is omitted, i.e., that it ﴿does not return to them a word﴾, i.e., it does not give them a reply; ﴿nor does it control for them any harm﴾, i.e., its repelling, ﴿nor any benefit﴾, i.e., its bringing about. So how could they take it as a god?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 90:

﴿And Harun had already said to them before this﴾, i.e., before Musa returned: ﴿O my people, you are only being tested through it. Indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in His worship ﴿and obey my command﴾ concerning it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 20, verse 91:**

﴿They said, "We will never cease to be devoted to it"﴾, meaning: "نَزال" (we will not cease) ﴿devoted to it﴾, meaning: "عَلى عِبادَته" (to its worship), "مُقِيمِينَ" (remaining).

Musa said, after his return: "O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,

[from following me?]"

Wait, I should not add. Translating exactly:

Musa said, after his return, "O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from worshipping [Him alone]..."

Let me give the faithful version without additions beyond what the text contains:

Musa said, after his return: "O Harun, what prevented you when you saw them going astray" by worshipping it.

Harun said: "O son of my mother!" (with the mim read both with a kasra and with a fatha; he meant "my mother," and mentioning her is more tender to the heart). "Do not seize me by my beard" (he had seized it with his left hand), "nor by my head" (he had seized his hair with his right hand, in anger). "Indeed I feared" (that if I followed you, a group of those who had not worshipped the calf would surely follow me) "that you would say: 'You have caused a division among the Children of Israel'" (and be angry with me), "and you did not observe" (did not await) "my word" (concerning what I had seen in that matter).
﴿He said, "Then what is your affair?"﴾ Your matter, the thing that prompted you to what you did.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 96:

﴿He said: "I perceived what they did not perceive, so I took a handful from the footprint of the Messenger"﴾ with the verb read with ya' and with ta' (i.e., "they perceived" / "you perceived"), meaning: I knew what they did not know. ﴿So I took a handful﴾ of dust ﴿from the footprint﴾ of a horse's hoof ﴿of the Messenger﴾, meaning Jibril (Gabriel). ﴿Then I threw it﴾, I cast it, ﴿in the form of the molded calf﴾ ﴿and thus my soul enticed me﴾, adorned it for me. And it was inspired into me that I should take a handful of the dust mentioned and cast it upon something that has no spirit, and it would come to have a spirit. And I saw your people asked you to make for them a god, so my soul suggested to me that this calf should be their god.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 97:

﴿He said﴾ to him (Musa), ﴿"Go, then"﴾ away from among us, ﴿for indeed, it is yours in the life﴾, i.e., for the duration of your life, ﴿that you should say﴾ to whoever you meet, ﴿"No touching"﴾, i.e., do not come near me. So he would wander in the wilderness, and if he touched anyone, or anyone touched him, they would both be struck with fever together. ﴿And indeed, for you there is an appointment﴾ for your punishment, ﴿which you will not fail to keep﴾, with the kasra on the lam (tukhlifahu): i.e., you will not be absent from it; and with the fatha on it (tukhlifahu, read as "tukhlafahu"): i.e., rather, you will be sent to it. ﴿And look at your god to whom you remained devoted﴾, its original form being ẓalilta with two lams, the first of which is kasra and was dropped for lightness, i.e., you continued, ﴿devoted to it﴾, i.e., staying, worshipping it. ﴿We will surely burn it﴾ with fire, ﴿then we will surely scatter it into the sea, a scattering﴾, i.e., we will disperse it into the air of the sea. Musa did after slaughtering it what he mentioned.

Translation:

﴿Indeed, your God is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, He has encompassed all things in knowledge.﴾ "Knowledge" is a tamyiz (specification) transferred from the agent; that is, His knowledge has encompassed all things.

Thus (We relate to you, O Muhammad, this story), ﴿Thus﴾ meaning: just as We have related to you this story, O Muhammad, ﴿We relate to you some of the tidings﴾ news, reports ﴿of what has passed before﴾ of the nations, ﴿and We have certainly given you﴾ bestowed upon you ﴿from Us﴾ from Our presence ﴿a Reminder﴾ the Qur'an.
Whoever turns away from it (﴿مَن أعْرَضَ عَنْهُ﴾), and does not believe in it, then he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden (﴿وِزْرًا﴾), a heavy load of sin.

﴿Abiding therein﴾, that is, in the punishment of the burden. ﴿And evil is it for them on the Day of Resurrection as a burden﴾: "as a burden" is a tamyiz (specification) explaining the pronoun in "evil is it" (sā'a), and the thing being dispraised (al-makhsus bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its estimated form being "their burden" (wizruhum). The lam in "for them" (lahum) is for explanation (li-l-bayan), and "on the Day of Resurrection" (yawm al-qiyamah) may be read as a substitute (badal) for the preceding phrase.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 102:

﴿On the Day the Horn is blown﴾ the trumpet, the second blowing; ﴿and We shall gather the criminals﴾ the disbelievers; ﴿on that Day, blue-eyed﴾ their eyes being blue along with the blackness of their faces.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 103:

﴿They whisper among themselves﴾ (yatakhafatuna baynahum): they speak secretly to one another. ﴿"You stayed"﴾ (in), i.e. "what you remained" (in the world), ﴿"but ten"﴾ (illa ashran) nights, with their days.

We know best what they say about that: that is, it is not as they said. ﴿When their best in path says﴾, that is, the most just of them in their way, ﴿"You stayed only a day"﴾, they consider their stay in the world to be very brief, because of what they witness of the terrors of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 105:

﴿And they ask you about the mountains.﴾ (That is, how they will be on the Day of Resurrection.) ﴿Say:﴾ (to them) ﴿"My Lord will blow them away with a blast."﴾ (That is, by crumbling them into something like flowing sand, then scattering them with the winds.)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 106:

﴿So He will leave it as a level plain﴾ flattened, spread out, ﴿a smooth, leveled expanse﴾ even and level.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 107:

﴿You will not see in it any crookedness﴾ (i.e., depression) ﴿or any elevation﴾ (i.e., height)

On that Day they will follow the caller (al-Da'i) without any deviation (lit. crookedness) from him: that is, the people, after rising from their graves, will follow the one calling them to the place of assembly (al-Mahshar) with his voice, and he is Israfil, who says: "Come along to the presentation before the Most Merciful." There will be no crookedness in following him: that is, they will not be able to refuse to follow him. And the voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper: the sound of footsteps as they are led to the place of assembly, like the sound of camels' feet as they walk.

On that Day, intercession will not benefit anyone, except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted to intercede for him, and with whom He is pleased regarding his speech.

﴿On that Day, intercession will not avail,﴾ intercession will not avail anyone, ﴿except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾ to intercede on his behalf, ﴿and whose word He approves﴾ by his saying: "There is no god but Allah."
He knows what is before them [of matters of the Hereafter] and what is behind them [of matters of this world], but they cannot encompass Him in knowledge: they do not know that.

﴿And the faces will be humbled﴾ [i.e., submitted] ﴿before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all﴾, meaning Allah. ﴿And he who bears wrongdoing will have lost﴾, meaning he who bears wrongdoing, i.e., polytheism (shirk).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 112:

﴿And whoever does righteous deeds﴾, [that is,] acts of obedience, ﴿while he is a believer, he will not fear injustice﴾ by an increase in his bad deeds, ﴿or deprivation﴾ by a decrease in his good deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 113:

﴿And thus﴾ is conjoined to "thus We relate" (kadhalika naqussu): i.e., like the sending down of what has been mentioned. ﴿We have sent it down﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿as an Arabic Qur'an, and We have diversified﴾, i.e., repeated, ﴿in it some of the warnings, that perhaps they may be God-fearing﴾, i.e., may fear shirk, ﴿or it may give them remembrance﴾, i.e., the Qur'an may produce remembrance in them, through the destruction of the nations that came before them, so that they may take heed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 114:

﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth﴾ above what the polytheists say. ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾, i.e., with its recitation, ﴿before its revelation to you is completed﴾, i.e., before Jibril finishes conveying it. ﴿And say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge"﴾, i.e., of the Qur'an, so that whenever something of it is revealed to him, his knowledge of it increases.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 115:

﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam﴾ We had enjoined him not to eat from the tree ﴿before﴾ i.e., before he ate from it ﴿but he forgot﴾ he abandoned Our covenant ﴿and We found in him no resolve﴾ determination and patience regarding what We had forbidden him.

"And remember" when We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves before Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis. He was the father of the jinn; he used to accompany the angels and worship Allah with them. He refused ("abā") to prostrate to Adam, and said, "I am better than him."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 117:

﴿Then We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife﴾ Hawwa' (with the long vowel, ḥawwāʾ) ﴿so let him not expel you from the Garden, for you would then be distressed﴾ you would toil with plowing, planting, harvesting, grinding, baking bread and other things; and he confined the mention of distress to him, because the man is the one who strives for his wife.
﴿Indeed, for you﴾ an [ـ] ﴿not﴾

﴿وأنَّك﴾ (the hamzah, *hamzah* (glottal stop), in أنّ may be read with a fatḥah or a kasrah) is coordinated (*ʿaṭf*) with the noun of *inna* (اسم إنّ), and its clause is ﴿لا تَظْمَأ فِيها﴾, meaning "you will not thirst therein," that is, you will not become thirsty, ﴿ولا تَضْحى﴾, meaning "nor will you be exposed to the sun," that is, the scorching heat of the midday sun will not reach you, because there is no sun in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 120:

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ That is, the tree whoever eats from it will live forever. ﴿And a kingdom that does not decay﴾ that does not perish; and this is necessarily implied by eternity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 121:

﴿So they both ate﴾ of it, i.e., Adam and Hawwa' (Eve). ﴿Then their private parts became apparent to them﴾, i.e., there became visible to each of them his own private part (qubul) and the other's private part and rear (dubur). Each of them was called sawʾah (private part, that which must be covered) because its exposure distresses its companion (yasuʾu sahibahu). ﴿And they began to cover themselves﴾, i.e., they began to stick together ﴿over themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾, so that they might conceal themselves with it. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾, by eating from the tree.
﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾ brought him near. ﴿And turned to him﴾ before his repentance. ﴿And guided him﴾ i.e., guided him to persevere in repentance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 123:

﴿He said: "Go down"﴾, i.e., Adam and Hawwa', along with what your union has produced of your offspring, ﴿from it﴾, from the Garden, ﴿all of you﴾, ﴿some of you to others an enemy﴾, through the wrongdoing of some of them toward others. ﴿Then if﴾ (فَإمّا): in it there is idgham (assimilation, the merging of one consonant into another), where the nun of the conditional particle إنْ is assimilated into the added ما. ﴿There comes to you from Me guidance, and whoever follows My guidance﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿will not go astray﴾ in this world, ﴿nor will he be wretched﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 124:

﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿and does not believe in it, then indeed for him is a constricted life﴾. The word "ضَنْكًا" (ḍankan) is read with tanwin (nunation, the "-n" sound added to the end of a word), and it is a verbal noun with the meaning "ضَيِّقَة" (ḍayyiqah), i.e., narrow or constricted. It has been explained in a hadith as the punishment of the disbeliever in his grave. ﴿And We will gather him﴾ — i.e., the one who turns away from the Qur'an — ﴿on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ — blind in sight.
﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You raised me up blind when I was [once] seeing?"﴾ in the world and at the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 126:

﴿He will say﴾: The matter is ﴿thus: Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾, meaning you abandoned them and did not believe in them. ﴿And thus﴾, in the same way as your forgetting Our signs, ﴿this Day you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left in the Fire.

And thus (وَكَذَلِكَ): as We recompense those who turn away from the Qur'an, so We recompense ﴿whoever transgresses﴾ — that is, who commits shirk (associates partners with God) — ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord﴾. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is harsher﴾ than the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave, ﴿and more lasting﴾, that is, more enduring.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 128:

﴿Has it not become clear﴾ (yatabayyan) ﴿to them﴾, to the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿how many﴾ (kam, here an informative particle, object of) ﴿We destroyed﴾ (ahlaknā), that is, We destroyed many, ﴿before them of generations﴾, that is, the past nations, by their denial of the messengers. ﴿They walk﴾ (yamshūna), a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the pronoun in ﴿lahum﴾, ﴿in their dwellings﴾, that is, in their travels to Syria and elsewhere, so that they may take heed. What is mentioned here, namely "ahlaknā" (We destroyed) in the form of a verb without the verbal particle (ḥarf maṣdarī), is for the sake of the meaning, and there is no objection to it. ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ (la-ʿibar), ﴿for those of understanding﴾, that is, for those possessing intellects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 129:

﴿And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾ (namely) the postponement of the punishment for them until the Hereafter, ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾ (i.e., the destruction) would have been binding upon them in this world, ﴿and a specified term﴾ (that is) appointed for them, conjoined (ma'tuf) to the pronoun concealed (mustatir) in kana (it would have been), and the separation (al-fasl) by its predicate (khabar) took the place of emphasis (al-ta'kid).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 130:

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾ — abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of fighting (ayat al-qital). ﴿And glorify﴾ — pray (ṣalli). ﴿With the praise of your Lord﴾ — a circumstantial clause (ḥāl): i.e., while accompanied by it (mulTabisan bihi). ﴿Before the rising of the sun﴾ — the dawn prayer (ṣalat al-subh). ﴿And before its setting﴾ — the afternoon prayer (ṣalat al-'asr). ﴿And during the hours of the night﴾ — its times (sā'atihi). ﴿So glorify﴾ — pray (ṣalli): the sunset (maghrib) and night (ʿisha') prayers. ﴿And at the extremities of the day﴾ — a conjunction (ʿaṭf) on the grammatical position (maḥall) of "min ā'nā'" in the accusative: i.e., pray the noon prayer (ṣalli al-ẓuhr), because its time enters with the decline of the sun, so it is the extremity of the first half and the extremity of the second half. ﴿That you may be pleased﴾ — with what you are given of reward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 131:

﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that which We have given enjoyment to certain pairs of them﴾ (i.e., kinds) ﴿of the splendor of the life of this world﴾ (its adornment and its beauty), ﴿so that We may test them thereby﴾ (by making them transgress). ﴿But the provision of your Lord﴾ (in Paradise) ﴿is better﴾ than what they were given in this world ﴿and more lasting﴾ (more enduring).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 132:

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 20, verse 134:

﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, before Muhammad the Messenger, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs," the ones sent with him, "before we were humiliated," on the Day of Resurrection, "and disgraced," in Hell.﴾
